# Psalm 142 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A Prayer. With my voice I cry out to the LORD; with my voice I plead for mercy to the LORD.

**2** I pour out my complaint before him; I tell my trouble before him.

**3** When my spirit faints within me, you know my way! In the path where I walk they have hidden a trap for me.

**4** Look to the right and see: there is none who takes notice of me; no refuge remains to me; no one cares for my soul.

**5** I cry to you, O LORD; I say, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."

**6** Attend to my cry, for I am brought very low! Deliver me from my persecutors, for they are too strong for me!

**7** Bring me out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name! The righteous will surround me, for you will deal bountifully with me.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 142.

- **142:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **142:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **142:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **142:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **142:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **142:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **142:4**: 'There-is-no one-recognizing... no one-caring for my-soul' — the nadir of isolation; David in the cave with no human ally.
- **142:5**: 'You my-refuge, my-portion' — when all human refuge has perished, God himself becomes both shelter and inheritance.

### LOGOS
- **142:1**: The cave setting (1 Sam 22:1 or 24:3) gives this psalm its raw, enclosed, desperate quality. David is literally trapped.

### PNEUMA
- **142:4**: 'No one even notices me. I have nowhere to run. Nobody cares.' Three devastating statements in a row. This is what total isolation feels like — and the psalm doesn't pretend it away. It just redirects the cry to God.
- **142:7**: 'Free me from this prison so I can praise your name' — the motivation for rescue isn't comfort but worship. The psalmist's deepest desire isn't escape but thanksgiving.

— SOPHIA
